None of the common CLI mail tools are installed. Here are a few options you can use depending on what you install or have available:

### Option 1: Using `mutt`
```bash
sudo apt-get install mutt -y
echo "Please find the Customer Activity Report attached." | \
  mutt -s "Customer Activity Report" \
       -a testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf -- \
       bob@example.com
```

### Option 2: Using `swaks` (Swiss Army Knife for SMTP)
```bash
sudo apt-get install swaks -y
swaks \
  --to bob@example.com \
  --from your-email@example.com \
  --subject "Customer Activity Report" \
  --body "Please find the Customer Activity Report attached." \
  --attach testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf \
  --server smtp.example.com:587 \
  --auth LOGIN \
  --auth-user your-email@example.com \
  --auth-password "YOUR_PASSWORD" \
  --tls
```

### Option 3: Using `msmtp` + `mail`
```bash
sudo apt-get install msmtp msmtp-mta mailutils -y
# Configure ~/.msmtprc with your SMTP server details, then:
echo "Please find the Customer Activity Report attached." | \
  mail -s "Customer Activity Report" \
       -A testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf \
       bob@example.com
```

### Option 4: Node.js script (using `nodemailer`)
```bash
npm install nodemailer
```
```js
const nodemailer = require('nodemailer');

const transporter = nodemailer.createTransport({
  host: 'smtp.example.com',
  port: 587,
  secure: false,
  auth: { user: 'your-email@example.com', pass: 'YOUR_PASSWORD' }
});

transporter.sendMail({
  from: 'your-email@example.com',
  to: 'bob@example.com',
  subject: 'Customer Activity Report',
  text: 'Please find the Customer Activity Report attached.',
  attachments: [{ path: 'testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf' }]
}).then(() => console.log('Email sent!'));
```
